verdict.rationale: iTerm2 documents shell integration that tracks prompts, commands, history, directory and host, with marks at each prompt. It separately documents job-completion notifications and per-line timestamps that help gauge how long a job took. The evidence never mentions exit-status display, and it does not tie duration or notifications to shell-integration command tracking. missing for 10: exit status of commands, explicit per-command duration from shell integration, documentation linking completion notifications to shell-integration command boundaries, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I get command-aware features from shell integration, like exit status, duration, and notifications when long commands finish

citations.quote: iTerm2 can integrate with your shell so it knows where your shell prompt is, what commands you're entering, which host you are on, and what your current directory is.
You can choose to receive notifications of activity, bells, job completion, and more. Feel free to let a long job run in the background
You can see the last-modified time of every line in the terminal. It's useful to know how long a job took to complete
